messages:
Priya: quick heads-up — want to run a short design review tomorrow 11am PT on the trace panel action ordering + screen-reader labels. small scope: request drilldown header actions and stacktrace export placement :eyes:
Alex: SGTM. what's the current proposal?
Priya: prototype attached in Figma. key ideas: move primary action (Copy Correlation ID) to the left of the permalink, group exports into a kebab menu (Download trace / Download HAR / Export CSV), keep 'Open in new tab' on the far right. also add explicit aria-labels for each action.
Sam: flag: runtime needs the copy button to also include an event that surfaces which model/runtime served the request (for debugging). can we include a hidden data attr for that?
Maria: a11y nits: grouping into a menu is fine, but we must ensure the menu is keyboard operable and has proper aria-expanded/aria-controls. also screen reader text should announce "exports menu, n items". avoid relying on color or icon-only labels. :a11y:
Priya: noted. initial aria suggestion in Figma notes: use `aria-label="Copy correlation ID"` and `aria-describedby` for the tooltip text.
Alex: quick keyboard question — tab order should go: left actions -> center title -> right actions -> kebab menu. If kebab opens, first item should receive focus.
Devon: test cases: 1) tab through header actions with NVDA/VoiceOver 2) open kebab via Enter/Space 3) export HAR with large traces doesnt freeze UI 4) copy correlation ID includes copy-to-clipboard + toast + analytics.
Maria: additionally, for stacktrace collapse/expand buttons, add `aria-pressed` to convey state. and use `aria-live="polite"` on toast messages like "Correlation ID copied" so screen readers announce them.
Sam: runtime: for large traces the Export HAR job will be async. we prefer the UI to show "Preparing export" spinner and then email / in-app notification when ready. can we change the label from "Download" to "Request export" for big traces? avoids expectation of immediate download.
Priya: good call. UX suggestion: show two export affordances — quick export (small traces, immediate) and request export (large traces, async). label quickly as badges: "small trace" vs "large trace"? maybe too noisy. open to alternatives.
Alex: maybe detect size and change the primary export label dynamically. but we still need to expose the action so keyboard users see both options in menu.
Maria: if label changes dynamically, ensure `aria-live` announces that the option is now async. e.g., `aria-label="Export trace (async — will be available in notifications)"`
Devon: implementation notes for QA: add an e2e that stubs large trace export and validates notification flow. also test copy analytics event payload.
Priya: layout note — we debated moving the kebab into the trace inspector side panel vs keeping it in header. pros/cons in Figma comments: header keeps actions discoverable; side panel groups actions with exports/attachments. which do we prefer?
Sam: runtime ops: header is easier for quick workflows. but if we move to side panel we can preload export metadata. engineering prefers header for now unless design strongly favors otherwise.
Alex: header also helps with keyboard muscle memory. side panel would be ok if we add a visible affordance to open it quickly.
Maria: whichever we pick, ensure heading levels in side panel are semantic (h2/h3) and that the export section has a proper heading for screen reader navigation.
Priya: agreed. final asks for tomorrows review: 1) decision on header vs panel 2) precise copy for async export state 3) aria labels for copy/permalink/kebab 4) keyboard/focus behavior doc
Devon: I can draft the acceptance criteria and add to the PR.
Alex: I'll prototype the keyboard flow in the dev build and push a playground link before the meeting.
Maria: I'll prepare a quick NVDA checklist and sample copy for the aria labels.
ops-bot: Deploy bot: dev-playground updated at 1850001128 (branch: trace-actions-kebab).
Priya: perfect — thanks everyone. see you tomorrow 11am PT. :thumbsup:
